title: Health literacy and health behaviour in Germany in the age of AI
summary:
Health literacy refers to the ability to find, understand, critically appraise, and apply health-related information to make informed decisions. Due to digitalisation and, in particular, the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI), for instance, in the form of chatbots or automated symptom checkers, these requirements are fundamentally changing. While AI systems deliver rapid and linguistically accessible responses, they carry the inherent risk of incorrect or inappropriate advice. Digital health literacy therefore now also encompasses the skill to methodically question AI-generated content on health-related topics and concerns, assess its reliability, and recognise its limitations.

Surveys demonstrate that general and digital health literacy among the German population currently exhibit deficits. Given that a proficient handling of health information is linked to better health behaviour and the appropriate utilisation of healthcare services, healthcare stakeholders are calling for targeted support measures. The present study assesses the current status quo in Germany and analyses previously under-researched associations, with a central focus on the practical use of AI for health-related concerns.

interventions.name: This is a non-interventional cross-sectional study conducted via a standardized online survey.
